Extract from Japanese Newspapers Translation
20.11.31.
----------

Correction of Published Article

The Shanghai Nippo publishes the following
report:-

At the request of the Shanghai Municipal
Police the Shanghai Nippo hereby inserts the following
correction in connection with the article published
on November 9 to the effect that 3 drunken men entered
a certain cafe on Boone Road and brandished a dagger
etc.:

According to investigation conducted by the
Shanghai Municipal Police the drunken persons in question
only attempted to joke with the waitresses when they
exhibited their truncheon.

《上海日报》（Shanghai Nippo）刊登如下报道：-

应上海公共租界工部局警务处之请求，《上海日报》特此就11月9日发表的文章插入以下更正，该文章称三名醉汉进入百老汇路（Boone Road）某咖啡馆并挥舞匕首等物：

REPORT
Date Nov. 24, 1931

Subject (in full) Correction of News - Report in "Shanghai Nippo."

Made by C.D.I. Prince. Forwarded by

Sir,
On November 22, 1931 we approached Mr. Shuboshi, Editor
of the "Shanghai Nippo" and pointed out to him the inadequacy
of the correction published in his paper regarding the case of
alleged attempted stabbing, and he promised to reconsider the
matter when we pointed out to him that publication of articles
of this nature was detrimental to Japanese prestige. Now he
informs us that he considers the correction as published quite
sufficient and he does not propose to do anything further in
the matter.

（签名）
C. D. I.
Officer i/c Sp. Br.

Sir,

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
REPORT
Date November 20, 1931.

Subject (in full) Incorrect News Report in Shanghai Nippo

Made by and Forwarded by C.D.I. J.W. Prince.

Sir,
On November 15, 1931, we approached Mr. Shaboshi,
Editor of the Shanghai Nippo with a view to having a correction
inserted in the above newspaper regarding an incident, in which
three drunken Japanese were involved, an incorrect report on
which appeared in the Shanghai Nippo November 9 issue.
Mr. Shaboshi agreed to publish the correction which eventually
appeared in the above newspaper on November 19, 1931.
Please see translation of correction inserted
attached.

C. D. I.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

November 20, 1931. Morning Translation.

MISCELLANEOUS

CORRECTION OF PUBLISHED ARTICLE.
The Shanghai Nippo publishes
the following report:-
At the request of the Shanghai
Municipal Police the Shanghai Nippo hereby inserts
the following correction in connection with the article
published on November 9 to the effect that 3 drunken
men entered a certain cafe on Boone Road and brandished
a dagger etc.:-
According to investigation conducted by
the Shanghai Municipal Police the drunken persons in
question only attempted to joke with the waitresses
when they exhibited their truncheon.

RUSSIAN VOLUNTEER PATROL DESIRED IN EASTERN DISTRICT
The Shanghai Nippo publishes
the following report:-
Owing to the increase since
November 15 of stone-throwing at and abuse of Japanese
patrolling marines in the Eastern District by Chinese,
Mr. Fukushima, member of the Shanghai Municipal Council,
yesterday drew the attention of Mr. Fessenden, Secretary-
General of the Shanghai Municipal Council, to the state
of affairs. Instructions have been issued to both
the Yangtzepoo and Wayside Police Stations that in
future Japanese policeman must accompany Japanese marine
patrolling parties.
The Japanese residents in the
Eastern District are anxious to have the Russian S.V.C.
patrol the vicinity of Pingliang Road which district is
densely populated with Chinese.

PAN JAPANESE MEETING TO BE HELD ON DECEMBER 6.
The Shanghai Nippo publishes
the following report:-
At 5 p.m. yesterday, some 20
executive committeemen held a meeting at the Japanese
Club and decided to hold the Pan-Japanese meeting on
December 6, at the Central Japanese School.

CHINESE ASSAULTS JAPANESE GIRL STUDENT
The Shanghai Mainichi publishes
the following report:-
Yesterday morning a Japanese
girl student named Teru Takehana, accompanied by a
guardian, was proceeding to school on North Szechuen
Road near Wangpan Chao when she was assaulted by a Chinese
who struck her with a stick. Her guardian attempted to
arrest the assailant but he made good his escape into
Chapel.

东区希望组建俄国志愿巡逻队

如下报道：-
由于自11月15日以来，
东区中国人向巡逻的日本海军陆战队士兵投掷石块
及辱骂的行为增加，
上海公共租界工部局董事福岛（Fukushima）先生，

据11月9日《上海日报》称，11月8日上午
11时许，三名醉汉进入文路（即百老汇路）某咖啡馆，
饮酒后取出凶器，对女服务员施暴，并威胁
在场的美国客人。据分区警察局调查，前
述时间，三名醉汉进入文路2241号霍夫曼（Hoffman）咖啡馆，
饮酒后，其中一人从霍夫曼咖啡馆
拿出小木棍，试图戏弄女服务员，但并未发生
如报道所述的银两纠纷等事件。此外，该霍夫曼咖啡馆
虽雇佣了一名女服务员，但无人目睹此类轻率之事。
上述三人于凌晨3时离开该咖啡馆。

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 2888
Date 21. 11. 31）

The Shanghai Nippo of November 9, 1931, published an
article to the effect that at 1 a.m. November 8, three
drunken Japanese entered a certain cafe on Boone Road and
ordered drinks. After several drinks, one of them drew
a dagger from his pocket and attempted to stab a waitress
and threatened customers on the premises.

Investigations by the Municipal Police at all cafes
on Boone Road show that such an incident as stated in the
Shanghai Nippo did not occur. The Popular Cafe, 2258,
Boone Road, was visited by three unknown drunken Japanese
at about 1 a.m. November 8, who ordered drinks. After
several drinks one of the Japanese took a small wooden
truncheon from his pocket and started joking with a
waitress but no disturbance was caused. There are 8
waitresses employed at this cafe, but none of them saw
a dagger. The three men left the cafe at about 2 a.m.
the same date.
page_data.zh:
（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处
C. & S. B. 登记处
编号 S. B. D. 2888
日期 31年11月21日）

1931年11月9日的《上海日报》刊登了一篇文章，称11月8日凌晨1时，三名醉酒的日本人进入百老汇路（Boone Road）某咖啡馆并点酒饮用。几杯下肚后，其中一人从口袋中掏出匕首，企图刺伤一名女服务员，并威胁在场顾客。

工部局警务处对百老汇路所有咖啡馆的调查表明，《上海日报》所述的此类事件并未发生。11月8日凌晨1时许，三名身份不明的醉酒日本人光顾了位于百老汇路2258号的 Popular Cafe（大众咖啡馆），并点酒饮用。几杯下肚后，其中一名日本人从口袋中掏出一根小木棍，开始与一名女服务员开玩笑，但未引起骚乱。该咖啡馆雇有8名女服务员，但无人看到匕首。三人于同日凌晨2时左右离开咖啡馆。

REPORT

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE. C. & S. B. REGISTRY No. S. B. D. 2889 Honckew Station, Date 13. 11. 31. 1931）

Subject (in full) Translation of an extract from the Shanghai Nippo of Nov. 9. 1931.

Made by J.D.S. 50 Inouye. Forwarded by J Knight COT

Sir,
I beg to report that at about 1 a.m 6-11-31, three unknown drunken Japanese entered the Popular Cafe No. 3456 Boone Road, and ordered drinks.
After several drinks one of them took his small wooden truncheon and commenced joking with a waitress named I. Idegami.
No disturbance was caused. There are 3 waitresses, but not one saw a dagger. They left above cafe about 2 a.m. same date.
Inquiries were made at all of the Cafe Salons, Boone Road, but nothing in the nature of the report that appeared in the Shanghai Nippo could be discovered.

I am,
Sir,
Yours obediently,
S. Inouye
J.D.S. 50

先生，
谨此报告，31年11月6日凌晨1时许，三名身份不明的醉酒日本人进入百老汇路3456号 Popular Cafe（大众咖啡馆），并点酒饮用。

Translation of an extract from the
Shanghai Nippo of Nov. 9, 1931.

The Shanghai Nippo publishes the following
report:-

At 1. a.m. November 8, three drunken Japanese
entered a certain cafe in Boone Road and ordered
drinks. After several drinks one of them drew
out a dagger from his pocket and attempted to stab
a waitress and threatened customers in the premises.
He was stopped before creating further trouble.

It is however hoped that the authorities(?)
